newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rate worries seen capping SAfrica stocks near-term.
newsitem.headline: Rate worries seen capping SAfrica stocks near-term.

text.p: High domestic interest rates and a rising trend in rates in the U.S. are likely to cap the South African stock market over the next few months, according to the manager of South Africa's largest mutual fund.

"We see trading remaining low key until interest rates are cut sometime in the second half of the year," Jeremy Bolton, portfolio manager of Old Mutual Investors Fund, which has assets of 5.5 billion rand, said on Thursday.

"The advent of the start of the downturn in rates will provide the catalyst for the market to begin a new bull run. Prospects for 1998 are encouraging, particularly as the economy should be accelerating its growth phase."
But anxieties about U.S. rates could take its toll on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange and the participation of foreigners in the local markets was likely to lead to volatility.
"A sanguine view would be to buy equities later rather than sooner," Bolton concluded at a quarterly presentation on unit trusts.

The 10 best sectors on the JSE in the first quarter of 1997 were Copper (up 30 percent), Diamonds (up 21), Motors (up 19), Insurance (up 18), Stores (up 17), Building (up 17), Beverages (up 15), Property Trusts (up 14), Food (up 13) and Furniture (up 13).
